userStories.title: Add shared truncation and ranged file-read core
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Establish the single byte-safe model truncation policy, direction mapping, read ceiling, and reusable ranged file-read core.

**Motivation** — Tool output reaches the model through a byte ceiling and nothing else. There is no line cap, no per-line cap, and no way for the agent to recover what was cut.

**Approach** — Truncation is applied through `after_tool` rather than inside each tool, but the tools keep a bound on their own I/O. A two-tier split is required: if the model-facing cap left the tools entirely they would have to return unbounded content, trading a token problem for a memory one.

- **I/O ceiling (tool layer, a safety bound):** tools bound their reads to `READ_CEILING`.
- **Model-facing policy (`after_tool`, one implementation):** `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, `MODEL_MAX_LINES`, `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`.

**Constants** — `READ_CEILING` 2_000_000 bytes; `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` 40_000 bytes; `MODEL_MAX_LINES` 1_000 lines; `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS` 2_000 code units. The three model-facing caps must stay independently reachable: `MODEL_MAX_LINES * (MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS + 1)` must exceed `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, so a body can sit at the byte ceiling while still satisfying the line caps. At these values the product is 2_001_000 against a 40_000-byte ceiling.

**Precedence** — the three caps are independent triggers that compose as an ORDERED PIPELINE, never as alternatives. Being over one cap never buys a pass on another. (1) Per-line cap: shorten every line longer than `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`. (2) Line-count cap: if still over `MODEL_MAX_LINES` lines, the direction selects which lines to keep, chosen over the whole body rather than over a byte window of it. (3) Byte cap LAST: if the result still exceeds `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, cut on a codepoint boundary. Running it last is what makes the byte ceiling unconditional — nothing is appended or prepended after the cut. Under `tail-with-first-line` the first line is retained INSIDE that budget, not in addition to it; if it alone does not fit it is itself cut. `truncated` is true when any stage changed the content; `originalBytes` always reports the input's full UTF-8 byte length.

**Line counting** — a trailing newline TERMINATES the last line rather than opening an empty one, and an empty body has no lines, matching `readFileSlice`'s `totalLines` and `readTool`'s `[N lines]` header. `"a\nb\n"` is two lines, not three. A raw `split("\n")` breaks this in two places.

**Scope** — In: create the codepoint-safe truncator and shared ranged read core; add optional readCeiling; preserve `maxFileBytes` as the whole-file Edit/Write bound. Out: event registration (US-002), session/spill/paging integration (US-003), and deletion of legacy helpers (US-005).

**Interface** — Target: the same `ToolRunContext` shape, plus an **optional** `readCeiling?: number` — the tool's I/O bound, resolving to `READ_CEILING` when absent. Optional is load-bearing, not a style choice: 21 test files construct a `ToolRunContext` literal. `maxBytes` is retained and keeps its value, but is no longer consumed by any tool for truncation; the session's `after_tool` policy owns the model-facing ceiling. `maxFileBytes` is unchanged and remains the whole-file bound for `Edit`/`Write`.

**Patterns to follow:** `src/tools/scratchpad.ts:36-45` is the only correct codepoint-boundary slice in the codebase and is the base for the shared truncator. `src/tools/read.ts:78-137` is the precedent for `offset`/`limit` line semantics and the `[N lines]` header.
acceptanceCriteria: When `truncateForModel` receives a body within `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, `MODEL_MAX_LINES` and `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`, then it returns the body unchanged and `truncated` false.
When `truncateForModel` receives a body exceeding `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, then it returns `truncated` true and content whose UTF-8 byte length is at most `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`.
When a `truncateForModel` cut lands inside a multi-byte codepoint, then returned content has UTF-8 byte length at most `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` rather than exceeding it by emitting a replacement character.
When a body has more than `MODEL_MAX_LINES` lines while within the byte and per-line ceilings, then `truncateForModel` returns at most `MODEL_MAX_LINES` lines.
When a body contains a line longer than `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS` while within the byte and line-count ceilings, then `truncateForModel` shortens that returned line to that length.

When a body is within `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` but has both more than `MODEL_MAX_LINES` lines and a line longer than `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`, then `truncateForModel` applies both caps: the returned content has at most `MODEL_MAX_LINES` lines and no line longer than `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`.

When a body both exceeds `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` and carries a line longer than `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`, then `truncateForModel` returns content with no line longer than `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS` and UTF-8 byte length at most `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`.

When `truncateForModel` uses `tail-with-first-line` on a body exceeding `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, then returned content has UTF-8 byte length at most `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` and its first line is the body's first line, the retained first line counting against the byte budget rather than being added on top of it.

When `truncateForModel` receives a body ending in a trailing newline that is within every cap counting that newline as terminating its last line, then it returns the body unchanged and `truncated` false.
When `truncateForModel` uses `tail-with-first-line` on a body that ends in a trailing newline and exceeds `MODEL_MAX_LINES`, then the last retained line is the body's last non-empty line.
When `truncateForModel` uses `head`, then it returns the body's first lines and omits its last line.
When `truncateForModel` uses `tail-with-first-line`, then it returns the first line followed by last lines and omits middle lines.
When `truncateForModel` is called on a truncated or untruncated body, then `originalBytes` equals the body's full UTF-8 byte length.
When `truncationDirectionFor` receives `Bash`, `RunCommand`, or `Exec`, then it returns `tail-with-first-line`.
When `truncationDirectionFor` receives `Read`, `Grep`, `Git`, `ScratchpadRead`, or an unrecognised name, then it returns `head`.
When `readFileSlice` has neither `offset` nor `limit` and its file is smaller than supplied `readCeiling`, then it returns the whole contents and `bounded` false.
When a file is larger than supplied `readCeiling`, then `readFileSlice` returns `bounded` true.
When `readFileSlice` receives `offset` 3 and `limit` 2, then it returns the third and fourth lines.
When a file is within `readCeiling`, then `readFileSlice` returns `totalLines` equal to its line count.
When `readFileSlice` receives an offset greater than the file line count, then it returns empty content and that line count as `totalLines`.
When `readFileSlice` receives an `offset` of 0 or a `limit` of 0, then it rejects the request rather than returning the file's last line.

userStories.title: Introduce native loop event seam and result chokepoint
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add typed in-process `before_tool` and `after_tool` registrations and route every native tool-result message through one builder.

**Motivation** — The result is appended at seven separate sites in `turn-loop.ts`, so there is no single point at which a policy could be applied even if one existed.

**Approach** — The seam is built as **typed in-process function registrations**, not as an extension of `src/hooks/`, and not as a general eleven-event map. Two events are built because two have real consumers today: the spin breaker and invalid-call repair for `before_tool`, and the truncation policy for `after_tool`.

The dispatcher enforces four rules: **Results are partial patches, never mutations.** A handler returns only what it wants changed and the dispatcher merges. No handler receives the message array. **Handlers chain**, each seeing the previous handler's output, in registration order. **A throwing handler is logged at warn and skipped**, never failing the turn. **No handler may rewrite history.** `after_tool` is safe by construction because it shapes a result before it enters the array.

`before_tool` outcomes are `allow` (optionally rewriting the tool's input), `nudge` (prefixing the eventual result), `block` (answering without invoking the tool), and `terminate` (answering every outstanding call in the current batch). `after_tool` may patch `content` and `isError`. It may **not** patch `denied`: a refused Write is not a crashed Write.

**Scope** — In: dispatcher, result builder, spin/invalid migration, and exact synthetic-versus-genuine dispatch boundaries. Out: shared truncation/read primitives (US-001) and truncation/spill handler registration (US-003).

**Interface** — `before_tool` outcomes are `allow`, `nudge`, `block`, and `terminate`; `after_tool` patches only `content` and `isError`, never `denied`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `after_tool` is dispatched with no registered handler, then it returns payload `content` and `isError` unchanged.
When `after_tool` has two registered handlers, then the second receives the first handler's returned `content` as payload `content`.
When an `after_tool` handler throws, then the dispatcher logs at warn, skips it, and still applies a second handler patch.
When an `after_tool` handler returns only `content`, then the built message's `denied` value is unchanged.
When `before_tool` returns `allow` with `input`, then the tool is invoked with that input rather than the model's original arguments.
When `before_tool` returns `block`, then it produces a tool-result carrying handler content and does not invoke the tool.
When `before_tool` returns `terminate`, then it produces one tool-result for every outstanding call in the batch, each carrying handler content.
When `before_tool` returns `nudge`, then eventual tool-result content begins with handler text.
When `buildToolResult` returns a message, then it sets `toolCallId` on that message.
When the human Q&A budget is exhausted, then the turn pushes a tool-result and invokes no registered `after_tool` handler.
When no operator is reachable, then the turn pushes a tool-result and invokes no registered `after_tool` handler.
When an `AskHuman` call is answered, then the turn pushes the human answer and invokes no registered `after_tool` handler.
When the spin breaker stops the batch, then the turn pushes its notice and invokes no registered `after_tool` handler.
When policy denies a tool call, then the turn invokes a registered `after_tool` handler exactly once.
When a tool returns normally, then the turn invokes a registered `after_tool` handler exactly once.
When a tool throws, then the turn invokes a registered `after_tool` handler exactly once with `isError` true.
When a turn repeats an identical tool call past the spin threshold, then it answers every outstanding call in the batch and ends the loop, as it does today.
When a turn exhausts the invalid-call budget, then it ends the loop, as it does today.

routing.reasoning: This changes the central turn state machine, batch termination, and cache-sensitive transcript behavior.

userStories.title: Apply after-tool truncation, spill recovery, and scratchpad paging
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register shared truncation on native sessions, spill cut output to scratchpad, and make ScratchpadRead page full tool bodies.

**Motivation** — Tool output reaches the model through a byte ceiling and nothing else. There is no line cap, no per-line cap, and no way for the agent to recover what was cut.

**Approach** — Truncation is applied through `after_tool` rather than inside each tool, but the tools keep a bound on their own I/O. A two-tier split is required: if the model-facing cap left the tools entirely they would have to return unbounded content, trading a token problem for a memory one.

- **I/O ceiling (tool layer, a safety bound):** tools bound their reads to `READ_CEILING`.
- **Model-facing policy (`after_tool`, one implementation):** `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, `MODEL_MAX_LINES`, `MODEL_MAX_LINE_CHARS`.

`Read`, `Grep`, `Git`, `ScratchpadRead`, and unlisted names use `head`; `Bash`, `RunCommand`, and `Exec` use `tail-with-first-line`. Command output tails because the failure is at the end, but not naively: the body's first line carries the exit code, so the policy preserves that line and then tails.

On truncation only, the full body — up to `READ_CEILING` — is written at `spill/<toolName>-<callId>.txt`; the marker names the relative path and both byte counts. A body larger than `READ_CEILING` produces a spill file whose trailing line records that it is itself incomplete. The spill writer exposes filesystem calls through injectable `_spillDeps`, following `_scratchpadWipeDeps`; file writes use Bun-native APIs, not Node synchronous APIs.

**Scope** — In: register truncation handler, migrate model-facing tool truncation to read ceilings, add spills, and add ScratchpadRead offset/limit paging. Out: US-001 shared primitives, US-002 dispatcher/chokepoint, and US-005 helper deletions.

**Interface** — `scratchpadReadTool.inputSchema` target is its existing `{ type: "object", properties: { path }, required: ["path"] }` plus optional `offset` (1-based integer minimum 1) and `limit` (maximum line count, integer minimum 1), matching `readTool` spelling.

**Failure handling** — A spill write that fails → fail-open: the result is still delivered truncated, and the marker omits the spill path rather than naming a file that does not exist. A body exceeding `READ_CEILING` → the spill file is written up to the ceiling and records that it is itself incomplete. `ScratchpadRead` with an `offset` past the end of the file → returns a message naming the file's total line count, mirroring `readTool`'s behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: When a `Grep` result larger than `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` enters the message array, then its content UTF-8 byte length is at most `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`.
When a failing `Bash` command has stdout larger than `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, then its message-array result first line is the body's `exit N` line.
When that `Bash` result enters the message array, then its content ends with the body's final stderr lines.
When `Grep` output exceeds `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` but is smaller than `READ_CEILING`, then the tool returns the whole output before session policy runs.
When a tool result is truncated, then it writes `spill/<toolName>-<callId>.txt` under the scratchpad with the untruncated body.
When a `head`-directed tool result is truncated, then its content ends with a marker naming spill path, delivered byte count, and original byte count.

When a `tail-with-first-line` tool result is truncated, then that same marker sits immediately after the retained first line and any retained tail follows it, so its content ends with the body's final lines whenever the byte budget leaves room for a tail.
When a tool result is within every cap, then its scratchpad `spill` directory is empty.
When a spill write fails, then the result still enters the message array truncated and its marker names no spill path.
When a body is larger than `READ_CEILING`, then its spill file final line records that the spill is itself incomplete.
When a `ToolRunContext` omits `readCeiling`, then a tool bounds its read at `READ_CEILING` rather than `maxBytes`.
When `ScratchpadRead` receives `offset` 3 and `limit` 2, then it returns the third and fourth lines of the named scratchpad file and no other file lines.
When `ScratchpadRead` returns file content, then it begins with a `[N lines]` header reporting file line count, including when `offset` or `limit` is supplied; the header is not a file line.
When `ScratchpadRead` receives an offset past the last line, then it returns a message naming total line count.
When successive `ScratchpadRead` offsets read a spilled body larger than `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, then the whole body is recoverable.
When a native `Grep` call exceeds `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`, then `truncateForModel` is invoked once with its body and `head` direction.
When native `ScratchpadRead` receives `offset` and `limit`, then `readFileSlice` is invoked once with that offset and limit.
When a native tool result is within every cap, then the spill writer is not invoked.

routing.reasoning: It integrates event dispatch, several tool I/O migrations, and recoverable filesystem spills with fail-open behavior.

userStories.title: Wipe scratchpad after successful runs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make scratchpad cleanup run at successful completion and align scratchpad lifetime text.

**Motivation** — `src/prompts/sections/scratchpad.ts:27` already tells every agent that "Nothing there survives the run". That is false today: `wipeScratchpad` is called only at run start (`run-setup-init.ts:120`), so files survive until the next run's wipe.

**Approach** — Both wipes are kept, because they cover different failure modes. `cleanupRun` runs in a `finally` block, which does not run on SIGKILL, a hard crash, or power loss — so the start wipe remains the backstop that guarantees a clean slate however the previous run died. The end wipe is gated on `runCompleted === true`: a failed run retains its scratchpad for inspection, bounded because the next run's start wipe clears it.

**Scope** — In: add `dryRun: boolean` to cleanup options, pass runner dryRun, wipe only completed non-dry runs, and update prompt/tool text. Out: start-wipe behavior changes and cross-run coordination.

**Interface** — `RunCleanupOptions` target is its existing shape plus `dryRun: boolean`; the caller at `src/execution/runner.ts:395` has `dryRun` in scope and passes it through. `wipeScratchpad(workdir, opts?: { dryRun?: boolean }): Promise<void>` already tolerates absence and swallows failure at warn level.

**Failure handling** — An end-of-run scratchpad removal that fails → fail-open: logged at warn, `cleanupRun` still resolves, and run success is unaffected.
acceptanceCriteria: When `cleanupRun` receives `runCompleted: true` and `dryRun: false`, then it invokes scratchpad removal once with `<workdir>/.nax/scratchpad`.
When `cleanupRun` receives `runCompleted: false`, then it does not invoke scratchpad removal.
When `cleanupRun` receives no `runCompleted`, then it does not invoke scratchpad removal.
When `cleanupRun` receives `dryRun: true`, then it does not invoke scratchpad removal even when `runCompleted` is true.
When end-of-run scratchpad removal rejects, then `cleanupRun` resolves and logs at warn level.
When `wipeScratchpad` is invoked at run start, then it still removes the scratchpad directory regardless of any previous run outcome.
When `buildScratchpadSection` returns text, then it states the scratchpad is wiped when a run finishes and a failed run scratchpad is retained.
When `ScratchpadWrite` is advertised, then its description states the scratchpad is wiped when a run finishes rather than only at the start of each run.

routing.reasoning: This is a guarded integration with the existing fail-open wipe seam plus two text updates.

modifiedFiles.reason: pins the wipe as a run-start-only operation. Replacing invariant: the start wipe is unchanged and an end-of-run wipe additionally fires from `cleanupRun` when `runCompleted` is true and `dryRun` is false.

asserts the section's promise that nothing survives the run. Replacing invariant: the section states the scratchpad is wiped when a run finishes, retained after a failed run, and cleared at the next run's start.

userStories.title: Remove superseded tool truncators
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Delete per-tool truncation once after_tool is the only model-facing truncation seam.

**Motivation** — The truncation policy is reimplemented in five files that have already drifted: `read.ts:22-32`, `grep.ts:63-65`, `git.ts:327-329` and `scratchpad.ts:36-45` each carry their own `truncate()`, while `bash.ts:113` truncates inline with `body.slice(0, ctx.maxBytes)`.

**Approach** — US-003 already replaces every call into the five private truncators, so the deletions remove code that no test reaches by then; the build and lint gates are what confirm no reference survives.

**Scope** — In: delete superseded private Read/Grep/Git/Scratchpad helpers and Bash inline slice after US-003 migration. Out: changing US-001 policy algorithm or US-003 spill behavior.

**Interface** — `src/tools/truncate.ts` — created by US-001; the replacement every deleted helper defers to.
acceptanceCriteria: When a `Grep` result larger than `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` enters the message array after deletions, then its content UTF-8 byte length is at most `MODEL_MAX_BYTES`.
When a `Git` result larger than `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` enters the message array after deletions, then its marker names original byte count.

routing.reasoning: It removes duplicated code across existing tools after the replacement integration is available.

suggestedCriteria: When a tool result is within every model cap after the deletions, then it is delivered without a truncation marker.

analysis:
Existing TypeScript code requires a cross-cutting migration. ToolRunContext defines a tool-owned maxBytes cap at src/tools/registry.ts:47-67 and createCodingToolRuntime constructs it at src/tools/runtime.ts:269-281. Preserve compatibility with the many literal test contexts by adding optional readCeiling and resolving absence to READ_CEILING. Duplicated output truncation exists in Read (src/tools/read.ts:22-32), Grep (src/tools/grep.ts:63-65), Git (src/tools/git.ts:327-329), ScratchpadRead (src/tools/scratchpad.ts:36-70), and Bash (src/tools/bash.ts:109-118). Grep drains ctx.maxBytes (src/tools/grep.ts:129-130), Git passes it to gitWithTimeout (src/tools/git.ts:381-389), and RunCommand/Exec also slice command bodies (src/tools/run-command.ts:443-445; src/tools/run-command-exec.ts:86-93); the migration must preserve a tool I/O bound while moving model shaping into native after_tool. bounded-io returns an overshoot byte (src/utils/bounded-io.ts:17-50), and ScratchpadRead has the sole codepoint-boundary precedent.

turn-loop.ts has seven inline tool-result pushes and inline invalid/spin policy (src/agents/native/session/turn-loop.ts:350-452). Only policy denial, normal tool answer, and caught tool throws are genuine executions; AskHuman budget/no-operator/answer and spin-stop are synthetic. Invalid-call repair currently returns rewritten transcript messages (src/agents/native/session/handle-invalid-tool-call.ts:48-128); the event seam must preserve observable repair/stop behavior without exposing history to handlers. TurnDeps owns spinBreaker (src/agents/native/session/turn-types.ts:54-104), so session/adapter wiring must own registrations. Existing tests include test/unit/agents/native/session/turn-loop-invalid-input.test.ts, turn-loop-invalid-input-budget.test.ts, and session-lifetime-spin.test.ts.

ScratchpadRead is path-only and tool-truncates at maxBytes (src/tools/scratchpad.ts:116-151); reuse Read's range semantics (src/tools/read.ts:78-137), retain pre-truncation metrics, and write recoverable spills within SCRATCHPAD_DIR. Spill filesystem dependencies must be injectable like _scratchpadWipeDeps (src/execution/lifecycle/scratchpad-wipe.ts:27-48). RunCleanupOptions has runCompleted but no dryRun (src/execution/lifecycle/run-cleanup.ts:51-82), and runner does not pass dryRun to cleanup (src/execution/runner.ts:395-417). wipeScratchpad already swallows and warns on failure (src/execution/lifecycle/scratchpad-wipe.ts:39-57); add it only after completed non-dry runs while retaining start wipe for crashes. Key risks are UTF-8 replacement-byte overflow, marker bytes exceeding the model cap, losing command stderr, naming failed spill files, invalid provider tool-call/result pairing, and cache-prefix rewrites. Implement US-001 and US-002 independently, then US-003, with US-004 independent and US-005 last.
outOfScope: The nine remaining in-loop events in pi's `HookMap` — `transform_context`, `before_request`, `before_payload`, `after_response`, `before_compaction`, `before_navigation`, `before_run`, `before_drive` and `before_run_end` — are not built.
`transform_context` specifically is excluded by design rather than omission: at a 96.7% prefix-matched cache-hit rate, a history-rewriting handler makes the workload roughly 5x more expensive.
Extending the orchestration hook subsystem under `src/hooks/` is not part of this work; those events fire around a story, shell out with a 5s timeout, and cannot carry a rewritten tool result.
Trimming the advertised tool set, and bounding `advertisedSchemaBytes` in `src/tools/provider-advertise.ts`, are deferred; they belong at advertise time rather than per call.
Making `readTool` populate `resultBytesPreTruncation`, which it never sets today, is deferred to a separate issue.
Cross-model thinking-block replay on a fallback model swap (nax#2150) is deferred; it shares no code with this seam.
Changing the compaction threshold or any model's configured `contextWindow` is not part of this work.
Two concurrent nax runs sharing one workdir's scratchpad directory is not handled; the run lock is assumed to prevent it.
